body.statement:
After matching the common selector-gated syntax,
\[
\Theta_H=\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\cap
\left\{\theta:\operatorname{supp}_{p_\theta}(S)=H,\ p_\theta(c)>0\text{ for every }c\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\right\}
\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+).
\]
The inclusion is strict whenever the published class contains a law violating at least one displayed restriction.  Moreover, \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\subseteq\Theta_H^2\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)^2\).  If a pair in \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\) assigns positive mass outside \(H\), has a zero admissible cell, or fails equality on some coordinate of \(O_H\), then that pair is not in \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).  Consequently the published failure relation alone does not imply membership in the fixed-support global-twin relation; if it contains any such pair, \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\not\subseteq\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).
body.justification: This inclusion comparison isolates the logical obstruction to importing a larger-class branchwise witness into the fixed-support completeness theorem.
body.gap: Theorem 5 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser certifies specified failure constructions in its published model, but it does not type every output as an exact-\(H\), full-joint-law twin in the restricted-support interior subclass.
body.consumer: Reviewers and implementers can distinguish a legal fixed-support nonidentification certificate from a witness that silently adds a context or preserves only part of the supplied joint table.
body.proof_tex:
Define
\[
 \mathcal R_H=
 \left\{\theta\in\Theta(G^+):
 \operatorname{supp}_{p_\theta}(S)=H,\quad
 p_\theta(c)>0\ \text{for every }c\in
 \mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
All probabilities in (1) are well defined because \(\textnormal{ass:finite-categorical}\) gives finite alphabets and the recursive SCM definition supplies \(p_\theta\).  By the definition of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\), its members satisfy the common recursive order, declared independent-root factorization, known selector multiplexers, and full canonical response-table parameterization, before either restriction in (1) is imposed.  By \(\textnormal{def:model-class}\), \(\Theta_H\) imposes precisely this common syntax together with the two restrictions in (1).  Hence
\[
 \Theta_H=\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\cap\mathcal R_H
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+).
\tag{2}
\]
If the published class contains a parameter violating either restriction in (1), that parameter belongs to the right side of (2) but not the left side, proving strictness under the stated premise.

By the definition of the support-exact global twin relation,
\[
 \mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}
 =\{(\theta^+,\theta^-)\in\Theta_H^2:
 O_H(\theta^+)=O_H(\theta^-),\ 
 T_{a,H}(\theta^+)\ne T_{a,H}(\theta^-)\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Taking Cartesian squares in (2) and using (3) gives
\[
 \mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}
 \subseteq\Theta_H^2
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)^2.
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(w=(\theta^+,\theta^-)\in\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\).  If either coordinate \(\theta^\varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon\in\{+,-\}\), assigns positive selector mass to some \(s_0\notin H\), then \(\theta^\varepsilon\notin\Theta_H\) by \(\textnormal{ass:exact-selector-support}\), so (3) implies \(w\notin\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).  If instead some \(c_0\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\) has \(p_{\theta^\varepsilon}(c_0)=0\), then \(\theta^\varepsilon\notin\Theta_H\) by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\), and the same conclusion follows.  Finally, if equality fails on a coordinate of \(O_H\), then \(O_H(\theta^+)\ne O_H(\theta^-)\), which directly violates (3).  Thus each of the three displayed defects excludes the pair from the fixed-support global twin relation.

The definition of \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\) does not add exact support \(H\), positivity on every cell in \(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\), or equality of the complete map \(O_H\).  Membership in that relation alone therefore does not imply membership in \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).  If it contains a pair with any one of the three defects, that pair belongs to
\[
 \mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}
 \setminus\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}},
\]
which proves \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\not\subseteq\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).
